newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. AFRICA GAUTENG RACING TO RESTRUCTURE, LIST ON JSE.
newsitem.headline: S. AFRICA GAUTENG RACING TO RESTRUCTURE, LIST ON JSE.

text.p: The horse-racing industry in South Africa's Gauteng province said on Tuesday the region's various clubs will be restructured into a single firm, Raceco, which will be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
The racing authority said in a statement that in a step to broadening ownership in the industry, black empowerment groups would be offered a 22.5 percent stake in Raceco.

"We believe that by reorganising, restructuring and consolidating the business of the racing industry into one company we will position the industry for growth and broaden its ownership," said Steward Lumka, chairman of the racing industry's interim board.

The operations to be combined in Raceco are the Turffontein Racing Club, Gosforth Park Turf Club, Newmarket Turf Club and the Totalisator Agency Board, together with various service companies under the Highveld Racing Authority.

According to a memorandum of understanding with the Gauteng provincial government, the rest of the stakes in Raceco will be split between the Racing Trust, which will hold a 30.0 percent stake, strategic investors and management with 20.0 percent, 15.0 percent for the public, 10.0 percent for the racing public and 2.5 percent for the employee share scheme.
Raceco also intends to diversify its operations by applying for gambling and gaming licences.

"We believe that by combining horse racing with other forms of gambling we will be able to create an entertainment experience on the racecourse, which would help increase on-course attendance," Lumka said.
A shortlist of potential black investors in Raceco will be announced on October 3.
